label: bm-mamou-mani-portfolio
topic: Mamou-Mani Architects: what they build and how
summary: Fetched about 30 pages of the practice's own site, 19 Fab.Pub pages and 7 press pieces on 2026-11-12 as raw HTML (sha256 in data/mamou-mani/manifest.tsv) and extracted 77 verbatim-checked findings. The portfolio is larger and more varied than the earlier spec-partner-architecture record: about 30 listed projects from Cloud Capsule (2014) to Tate Modern (2025-26), in four material families: (a) PLA bioplastic printed on robot arms (Conifera 700 modules, Altostrata 12 modules, The Roe 30 x 20 kg modules, RIVA 3 x 1.9 m single print, Harmonic Tides, WOW!House); (b) timber and rattan (Galaxia 60 m x 20 m, 18,000 screws at 1.8 kN each; THK Tower 96 t ulin; Concordia; Catharsis); (c) sheet metal and ceramics (Smile, IWAN, Hermes facade, RIVA exterior); (d) sand (Sandwaves, 58 x ~160 kg). Fab.Pub has moved beyond PLA: recycled PETG (Neko Health Monolith Wall, 260 panels, 12 x 7.5 m, >800 robot-hours) and bamboo-filled PLA/PETG compounds (Tate), plus a named flame-retardant blend Fab.Shield. Philosophy in their words: designs 'emerge from the constraints of reality rather than through ego-led geometry'; the architect as 'a gardener'; circularity 'begins before a material is selected'. Pipeline: Rhino/Grasshopper, the open-source Silkworm G-code plugin (four co-authors), Dassault 3DEXPERIENCE, genetic algorithms, WASP printers (2018), robot arms and a shipping-container Mobile Factory. Material limits they state: PLA composts only industrially (60 C, 100% humidity, about a month), PLA is costlier than petroleum plastic and 'not very well researched', sand is weak, budget and time dominate temporary work. Moisture is almost unaddressed; fire is solved by additives with no published class; durability evidence is anecdotal (Conifera outdoors, WOW!House 3 years). Their sustainability numbers disagree: PLA carbon saving 68% (Dezeen 2019), 80% (several), 73.7% (computed from Aurora LCA), 75.5-83.7% (computed from the Altostrata per-kg figures); toxicity 30x vs 50x. Contradictions with earlier files are listed in findings F04, F13, F38, F39 and in recommendations. Not found: any item called Triumphant Fantasia, any Mamou-Mani project called Spiral (Galaxia is the spiral Burning Man temple), any measured water uptake, expansion or diffusivity, any fire class.
lay_summary: Mamou-Mani is a London architecture studio that designs shapes with computer code and then has them made, often by 3D printing in plant-based plastic. Think of a giant Lego-like canopy of 700 printed bricks, or a 60-metre timber temple built from ordinary planks and 18,000 screws and then burned on purpose. The studio says openly that its plastic has a built-in tension: it should last, yet it should also be able to rot away when you want it to. It publishes almost no hard numbers on water, sun or fire resistance, and one strength test is quoted in a unit that makes no physical sense. That gap is where a new, carefully measured material could be useful to them.

key_claims.claim: The practice itself states the central design contradiction: durable use versus biodegradability. PLA is chosen as a 'middle ground' that only composts industrially (founder, Frederic 2024, Dezeen 2019; Altostrata page 2023).
key_claims.evidence_quote: there is a contradiction between the idea of sustainable or durable and biodegradable, which is the opposite.

key_claims.claim: No quantitative moisture, UV, creep or weathering data are published by Mamou-Mani or Fab.Pub. Durability evidence is qualitative: Conifera modules left outdoors, WOW!House reused 3 years 'hasn't changed', Altostrata 'engineered to ... resist weathering'. The only moisture sentence concerns composting.
key_claims.evidence_quote: Outside are more Conifera modules, deliberately exposed to wind and rain to prove the longevity of PLA

key_claims.claim: Fire is handled by additives per project (Roe 'compounded with fireproof materials', RIVA 'non-toxic fire retardant', Fab.Shield blend) and no fire class or test result is published.
key_claims.evidence_quote: The interior piece was 3D printed robotically from a blend of fermented sugar and non-toxic fire retardant.

key_claims.claim: The only structural test on any practice page is one in-house pull test reported in an invalid unit (500 kg.m2); the founder concedes PLA is 'not very well researched'. A machine-checked, unit-correct property envelope would be new to them.
key_claims.evidence_quote: Our in-house tests with ARUP and Fab Pub have proven a resistance to pull forces of 500 kg.m2.

table.name: Stated material limits, by topic
table.fields: moisture=only end-of-life sentence (humidity speeds composting); fire=additive compounding (Roe, RIVA, Fab.Shield), no class published; durability=qualitative (Conifera outdoors, WOW!House 3 yr unchanged, Altostrata 'resist weathering'); recyclability=take-back crush-pelletise-reprint, conditional; industrial compost 60 C/100 % humidity/1 month; scale=Altostrata 2.7 m modules, Roe 20 kg modules, RIVA 3 x 1.9 m single print, Monolith 12 x 7.5 m; cost=PLA more expensive than petroleum plastic, Galaxia 'every penny' fundraised, min Fab.Pub order GBP 250 / 2 weeks; strength=sand weak (Sandwaves), PLA under-researched, one invalid pull-test unit

recommendations: Lead with their own sentence: 'there is a contradiction between the idea of sustainable or durable and biodegradable' (Frederic 2024; also the Altostrata page). Propose a material whose stability and decay are both specified and measured.

Offer what they lack: a unit-correct datasheet (modulus, strength, water uptake, expansion per % moisture, softening temperature) with test methods. Their only structural number is '500 kg.m2' and they say PLA is 'not very well researched'.

Moisture is the open ground: the practice has never published uptake or movement of its PLA blends, and their wood-, bamboo- and paper-filled blends (Fab.Grain, Fab.Zen, Paper PLA) are exactly the class known to be hygroscopic. Ask whether they treat that movement as a defect. A bilayer with the proved 3/2 curvature ceiling is a deliberate use of it.

Design the proof of concept to match their module culture: interlocking modules, reversible joints (cable ties, slotted shells, male/female connections), translucent or filled finish for backlighting, lattice infill tuned for weight, stiffness and light (as they did for the Tate platforms). Deliver the Grasshopper definition.

Match the process gap honestly: they print on robot arms with pellets and filament (PLA, PETG, filled blends), not resin or powder. Formlabs prints prove geometry and mechanism; a second step on Fab.Pub's extruder is needed to show their loop (crush, pelletise, reprint). Their stated minimum is GBP 250 and 2 weeks.
Do not quote their carbon percentages as fact; cite the Aurora LCA figures with the computed 73.7% and note the three other values.
Questions to ask them directly: fire classification of Roe/RIVA modules; the meaning of '500 kg.m2'; what Conifera modules did after outdoor exposure; whether Fab.Shield has a test report.
